For each organization, confirm at least 3 concrete ways it serves the community from its own site or other strong public pages, and note whether there is a visible way for an outsider to get involved through volunteering, donating, attending, or partnering; if something is not shown, say not shown. As you work, keep the strongest evidence tabs open for at least 6 organizations, including a mix of program, impact, and volunteer or support pages, so I can review them later. Then synthesize what you found into a comparison that groups the organizations by service model, points out the most common and the most distinctive community-service approaches, and recommends the 5 strongest organizations for someone who specifically wants hands-on community impact through jazz. In the final write-up, include a ranked top 5 with a short reason for each choice and make clear which organization looks best for volunteering, which looks best for youth education impact, and which looks best for broader community outreach.

Education and Community Engagement

Music education is at the core of our mission to protect, preserve and perpetuate New Orleans musical traditions. Passing on the knowledge of this music to the next generation of New Orleans musicians is a primary focus of the Preservation Hall Foundation, as well as a personal focus and passion of many of the beloved musicians of Preservation Hall. 

Over the COVID-19 pandemic, we launched Preservation Hall Lessons, offering students and educators free digital learning materials and classroom-ready lesson plans on New Orleans music and culture. Today, we are thrilled to resume in-person education programming like Kids in the Hall at Preservation Hall, and in partnership with music organizations around the country – providing unforgettable, experiential settings for students, learning by playing, and experiencing lasting mentorship with musicians, tradition bearers, and teaching artists from the Preservation Hall collective of musicians.

DONATE THROUGH GIVENOLA DAY!
SUPPORT NEW ORLEANS MUSIC EDUCATION→
Programs
Learning the New Orleans Way: 
Preservation Hall Lessons

The Preservation Hall Foundation has developed Preservation Hall Lessons: a free, online resource bank for teachers and music educators. The Lessons website includes a range of complete lesson plans for grades K-12, focusing on New Orleans style music, particularly traditional New Orleans Jazz and brass band music. The Lessons website is not just for regional use – it is now available for educators across the nation to help articulate the living art forms that exist in New Orleans on a national level, and ensure its inclusion in music education.

EXPLORE PRESERVATION HALL LESSONS
SUBSCRIBE FOR EMAIL UPDATES ON PHLESSONS
Brass Bandbook

The Preservation Hall Foundation Brass Bandbook is a free online resource for musicians and educators – complete with sheet music of 12 classic New Orleans tunes, like “Bourbon Street Parade and “Lil’ Liza Jane.” Complete with lyrics and historical context of the songs, this free sheet music is available for clarinet, trumpet, trombone, tuba, tenor sax, snare drum and bass drum at preshallfoundation.org/brassbandbook. 

ACCESS THE BRASS BANDBOOK→
Kids in the Hall

Classroom lessons come to life with the Preservation Hall Foundation's Kids in the Hall Field Trip program. In this one-hour field trip, students engage and listen to a Preservation Hall Band, as well as have an opportunity for a Q&A session with members of the Preservation Hall Collective. 

SIGN UP FOR A KIDS IN THE HALL FIELD TRIP →
Workshops, Masterclasses, and Open Soundchecks 

The Preservation Hall Foundation provides workshops, masterclasses, and open soundchecks to schools in the Greater New Orleans area and around the U.S., focusing on Brass Band and Traditional New Orleans Jazz. Open soundchecks are offered on 100% of the Preservation Hall Jazz Band's touring dates.  

To schedule a workshop or masterclass or to join us at an open soundcheck on any of Preservation Hall Jazz Band’s tour dates, email info@preshallfoundation.org.

Community Concerts

Community Concerts provides a range of free concerts in the Greater New Orleans area for communities limited in access to Preservation Hall by distance, economics, or other circumstances. These free concerts are performed by members of the Preservation Hall Collective and are designed for the whole family to attend. 

Stay tuned to our Facebook page for more details about upcoming concert performances. 

FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK →
FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM →
Sousafund

In the wake of Ben Jaffe's Sousaphone being stolen, the Sousafund was established in 2018 to provide young bass and sousaphone students with high quality instruments. Students in Orleans and Jefferson Parish have received instruments and mentorship on upright bass or sousaphone.

Seattle JazzED Programs Overview:

About/ Academic Year Programs/ Events/ Learning Resources/ JazzED + Schools/ Support/ Contact
Programs Overview
Programs
JazzSprouts

JazzSprouts is a jazz education program designed for children 8 months to five years old. Our 45-minute classes engage both the child and caregiver, through live music, dancing, story time and a racially-diverse curriculum. Families learn about core musical concepts, instruments, and great performers of Jazz, a vital Black American art form.

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Jazz Jumpers

Students K-3 will explore the core elements of music through the lens of jazz. Through singing, movement, and hands-on instrument discovery, young musicians will learn about the rich history of artists, their iconic styles, and the cultural roots that shaped this uniquely American art form.

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Foundations

Our Foundations class is for beginners in grades 4-8 with no previous music experience! Your budding musician will learn in with others in instrument groups built for individual learning and relationship building. We’ll teach you what you need to know about your instrument of choice in this class designed to support your musician for as many quarters as they need to feel confident on their instrument!

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Connections

Connections is for intermediate students in grades 5-8 who are proficient on their instrument and ready to grow as a jazz musician. Students will get lots of time to play their instrument. Classes focus on learning easy jazz tunes by ear, focused listening, ear-training, exploring rhythmic and creative concepts, and more!

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Explorations

Explorations is designed for musicians in grades 9 and above and is all about, well, exploring! Now that you are comfortable making music with your instrument, is there a particular topic that seems interesting? Maybe you want to play gigs but don’t know how to start, or maybe you want to dig in to modern jazz, or Latin music! Explorations includes a variety of classes of varying skill levels, so there’s something for everyone.

Seattle JazzED About Us text:
 REGISTER FOR FALL PROGRAMS TODAY!

 
About/ Academic Year Programs/ Events/ Learning Resources/ JazzED + Schools/ Support/ Contact
About Us
Seattle JazzED is YOUR home for excellent music education. 
We believe any student who wants to play should get to play. Maybe that’s you?

A bit about us. At Seattle JazzED we welcome students in grades K-12 at all levels. You can play or sing in an ensemble, take a one-day workshop, spend a week in the summer honing skills…or all three!

You may already know Seattle JazzED from some of our one-of-a-kind programs: The New Works Ensemble directed by composer Wayne Horvitz; or the Femme Ellington Project, Seattle's premier all-city girls' jazz band; or maybe Summer Jazz Ambassadors, a tour-de-force ensemble with training in performance skills and mentoring. 

Or maybe you’ve never heard of us until now. That’s cool too!

Here’s what you need to know: Any student can start their instrumental or vocal music education at Seattle JazzED and continue through high school graduation. We’ll take you the whole way. 

Do you already play music, or sing, and have for years? We’ve got plenty of opportunities for you too. 

If you need help figuring out where you fit in, contact us. We’d love to help you. 

P.S. Don’t let cost keep you from participating. At Seattle JazzED you always choose your tuition level. Flexible payment plans and full tuition waivers are also available, no questions asked. We’re able to offer sliding scale prices because our community of families pay what they can and our community of donors give what they can.  

You might be wondering: Why should I play jazz?

Good question! So glad you asked. We love jazz*  because it’s a quintessential Black American art form shared across America and the world. 

What’s more, in jazz you get to improvise and interpret music. It’s a powerful way to express yourself! With jazz you collaborate with your bandmates—you are responsible to each other and the performance you’re working toward. Because jazz is an improvisational music, you get comfortable with taking some creative risks and trying out new ideas. Jazz requires you to get curious, focus in and listen closely to your peers (and they’ll do the same for you.)

[For more on ‘Why Jazz’, watch the video with Wynton Marsalis above. IT’S GOOD.] 

Plus we have a lot of jazz history here! As a JazzED student you’re in league with Seattle’s rich jazz tradition, which stretches from Seattle’s early Jackson Street jazz scene with Ray Charles, Quincy Jones, and Ernestine Anderson, to the smooth jazz of Kenny G, through to the improvisational jazz of Wayne Horvitz, Bill Frisell, and Industrial Revelation. You can be part of this legacy. We’d love to have you.

                                Jazzmobile's mission is to present, preserve, promote and propagate America's classical music, Jazz. Founded in 1964 by National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Master, pianist, Dr. Billy Taylor and philanthropist and arts administrator, Ms. Daphne Anstein, Jazzmobile is the first U.S. not-for-profit arts and cultural organization created just for Jazz.  Since the beginning, we have been bringing high quality Jazz performances and education programs to area residents, tourists and other visitors, reaching over 4,000,000 people living or visiting New York City. Our national programs brought us to other cities in the US; and the 'Super Jazz Band' had us touring cities in Europe and Japan.
                                Whether on the street, in a park or at a major concert hall here or abroad, Jazzmobile works in partnership with like-minded organizations to present high quality Jazz performances that enrich the culture and imbue new life into the surrounding area. 
                                Our workshops, master classes, lecture demonstrations, and arts enrichment programs train the next generation of Jazz vocalists and musicians; while also exposing youth to this vibrant art form. For jazz aficionados and other enthusiasts, our panel discussions increase the knowledge of our many adult followers. Our primary aim is to reach out to communities where Jazz was nurtured and new forms born.
                                We are very proud of being an inspiration to other organizations such as The Manchester Craftsman's Guild and Jazz at Lincoln Center.

                                    New York City's longest continuous Jazz Festival : SUMMERFEST | Over 50 Years--We commissioned Wycliffe Gordon to create new music to the silent film 'Within Our Gates' by African-American filmmaker Oscar Micheaux. It was premiered with a live orchestra in August 2011 at Columbia University's Miller Theatre and we presented it again in 2013 at Symphony Space where it was recorded.  On April 1, 2016 - Gordon released his long awaited soundtrack Within These Gates of Mine.
                                    The first JAZZ performance at Lincoln Center Out-of-Doors--Under the direction of Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts Leonard de Paur, the creator of Lincoln Center Out of Doors, we presented its 1st Jazz program in 1964. 
                                    The Winnipeg Art Gallery Program
                                    1980 Winter Olympic Games, Lake Placid--NEA Jazz master (saxophone) Frank Foster (1928-2011) was commissioned to compose 'Lake Placid Suite' which was premiered during the Olympic games.  It was later broadcasted via live satellite on Billy Taylor's  NPR 'Jazz Alive,' with a performance by the 23 piece Jazzmobile All-Star Orchestra.
                                    Silver Bridge Concert celebrating Sister Cities New York and Tokyo--A once in a lifetime celebration performance at Lincoln Center's Alice Tully Hall.
                                    'Super Jazz Band' International and National Tour produced by Jazzmobile
                                
                            
                            Our concerts featuring acclaimed performers make musical magic, bringing Jazz to the streets and schools, parks and performance halls.                             Jazzmobile's multifaceted Jazz programming is the vehicle employed to support our mission while joining other arts organizations that are also affecting a positive economic impact on the communities we serve.
                            For over 50 years, we have brought Jazzmobile performance programs featuring acclaimed and emerging artists to neighborhood streets, parks, and community and senior centers in all five boroughs of New York City as well as local Harlem venues.
                            Are you a professional Jazz musician looking to take it to the next level? Do you enjoy singing or performing Jazz just for fun? Or are you seeking instruction for your child or school classes? Are you a lifelong student of Jazz and want to know the historical influence and the latest trends in today's Jazz music? Jazzmobile offers a variety of Jazz education programs for professional artists, New York City public school students and Jazz enthusiasts. Here, those who teach also do: many of our most popular Jazz performers also serve as our instructors.
                            Jazzmobile's core programs have become the model that others emulate across the United States.
                        
                        
                            One of our most popular annual events during SUMMERFEST is 'Great Jazz on the Great Hill' in beautiful Central Park. Each year, in partnership with the Central Park Conservancy we turn Central Park's Great Hill into a huge jazz 'Hall' complete with a wooden dance floor!
                            A Brief HistoryCreated by Jazzmobile nearly 25 years ago, the first Great Jazz on the Great Hill concert was in tribute to the legendary Charlie Parker, also known as Byrd. Johnnie Garry, Jazzmobile's Production Coordinator for 30 years until 2012, wanted to celebrate the birth of his good friend a true legend who died way too young.
                            For two years Jazzmobile presented GJGH. The festival later switched to the hands of the Charlie Parker Foundation. They moved this celebration of 'Byrd' downtown. After several years of producing the festival with the CPF, Johnnie suggested they add a second day with a concert at Marcus Garvey Park.
                            After being dormant for 14 years, Robin Bell-Stevens and John Reddick (Assistant Vice President, Central Park Conservancy) met and together worked to bring back Great Jazz on the Great Hill. And on August 5, 2017 the 10th anniversary of GJGH will be presented.
                            TodayOver 5,500 men, women and children from neighborhoods near, far and wide converge on the Great Hill with family and friends for a 3 hour festival of great jazz! Bring a blanket or lawn chairs and a cooler for a true "New York City moment." The audience comes with their picnic basket or they enjoy the delicious options from mobile food vendors while enjoying 'A List' swing bands, vocalists, Latin, and blues bands.  Many take to the special dance floor right next to the stage.  For children and their families, there is always a special activity that is showcased during the festival!
                        
                        
                            Do you think you're the best Jazz singer in New York City? In 2004, Jazzmobile, Inc. was invited by (jazz singer) Cynthia Holiday to launch the " Best of the Best" Jazz Vocal Competition with the generous support of Anheuser-Busch Companies.
                            Contestants vie for the top spot in front of judges and a live audience. Winners are selected by a panel of industry professionals, including singers, producers, and radio personalities. Many of the winners and finalists have acknowledged Jazzmobile for launching their careers. Our list of competitors and winners are performing locally, nationally and internationally, singers such as the first winner, in 2004 French jazz vocalist  Elisabeth Kontomanou. Other 1st place winners and top scorers have included:
                            Gregory Porter
                            Charenee Wade
                            Queen Esther
                            Lynette Washington
                            Brianna Thomas
                            Emily Braden
                            Alexis Cole
                            The Jazzmobile Vocal Competition is scheduled to return  in 2017.
                        
                        
                            For 5 years Jazzmobile partnered or collaborated with The Apollo Theater Foundation, Harlem Stage | Gate House and Columbia University to present the HARLEM JAZZ SHRINES FESTIVAL. When it debuted May, 2011, JAZZ SHRINES became "The Apple's" latest entry into the annals of what makes New York the epicenter of the jazz global.
                            This 7-day festival celebrated the classic clubs and venues that made Harlem USA the jazz mecca - beginning in the 1920's. The festival serves to reimagine clubs such as Minton's Playhouse, Lenox lounge, the Savoy Ballroom, and The Palace. While it's a nostalgic look back at the greatness of the past, this festival's pulse is the present, showcasing an array of today's top and emerging talent and showing that what's happening right now in Harlem really is where it's at!
                            Today Jazzmobile also applauds todays Harlem Shrines including others that are emerging in Harlem every year 'such as Showman's, Minton's Restaurant, Ginny's Supper Club, Sapphire, Paris Blues and the list keeps growing! Plans are underway for a festival celebrating the jazz shrines of Harlem, 2017!
                        
                        
                            Think of Jazzmobile and you probably think of our free Summerfest mobile Jazz concerts, attended by tens of thousands of people annually from the New York Metropolitan area, tourists and other visitors. Together with our partners' neighborhood associations and the NYC Department of Parks and Recreation Jazzmobile has brought top talent to under-served communities where many residents cannot afford to purchase tickets to the clubs and concert halls downtown. In addition to our neighborhood Jazz concerts our performances are held in large outdoor venues, such as Brooklyn Bridge Park, Grant's Tomb, Marcus Garvey Park and Central Park, drawing audiences from other boroughs and communities outside New York City.
                            Summerfest 2017 kicks off on July 5th and comes to a close on August 30th at Grants Tomb on Riverside Drive and West 122nd Street.  Watch for summer season announcement in April 2017during National Jazz Appreciation Month!
                        
                        
                            
                                'The Subject is Jazz' began as a televised Jazz music appreciation program created by Jazzmobile Co-Founder, Dr. Billy Taylor in the mid-1950s.  Little did he know that about10 years later it would become the genesis for one of Jazzmobile's core Jazz programs, 'Lecture Demonstrations: Jazz in the First Person.'
                                In 1968, Dr. Billy Taylor developed a jazz appreciation curriculum to expose New York City elementary, junior high, and high school students to Jazz as an art form. School music programs come and go and often ignore Jazz. As funding allows, talented Jazzmobile performers descend on schools across the city, conducting free, 45 to 60 minute musical and oral Jazz presentations that include:
                            
                            
                                the history and evolution of Jazz
                                an introduction to the instruments; and the creators of the music: the composers and musicians
                                a question and answer session with students and their teachers
                                o	an interactive live performance by jazz greats including legends and masters enabling the students to also participate with what they learned.
                            
                        
                        
                            Part of our education programs: 'The Subject is Jazz,' Jazzmobile's Saturday Jazz Workshops were started in 1969. The sessions brought aspiring artists together with Jazz masters like Dr. Billy Taylor and Cecil Bridgewater and other talented performers in a supportive learning environment. It has been located and various New York City Public schools including the Wadleigh Secondary (High) School for Visual and Performing Arts in Central Harlem. SJW has attracted more than 8,000 students of all ages since it began. Many of our graduates have gone on to successful musical careers. The program attracts a diverse student population from the five-boroughs of New York City, nearby New Jersey, Southern Connecticut, Long Island, and Westchester County.
                            Students develop their technical and performing skills in:
                            
                                harmony and theory
                                reading proficiency
                                composition
                                instrument technique development
                                ensemble and improvisational playing
                            
                            In FY 2016-2017 SJW is focusing on young emerging jazz students still in school.
                        
                        
                            Jazzmobile's Symposia and panel discussions is one of our The Subject is Jazz education programs. This program brings together some of the brightest minds in Jazz music, from acclaimed artists to academics to critics; exploring historic and emerging issues in Jazz culture. Held in partnership with esteemed institutions, our seminars and panel discussions offer interesting takes on issues surrounding the music. Here is a sampling of previous programs:

                                    Oscar Peterson - Style & Analysis

Clef Preparatory Jazz Music Academy

One of the great facts about jazz is that it bridges generations. Jazz relies on interactive improvisation and live performance, and thus can’t completely be taught in a classroom or with a book, aspiring younger musicians seek the direct guidance of older, wiser ones. Mentorship is crucial when passing on artistic genre to youth so the Philadelphia Clef Club of Jazz sees the component as a vital variable of its programs.  Mentoring fosters substantive one-to-one communications between student musicians and experienced master-level professionals.


Clef Prep Jazz Music Academy (CPJMA )
FALL TRIMESTER: A Deep Dive into Jazz Improvisation

“Exploring the Art of Spontaneous Musical Conversation”
Saturday, October 11, 2025 – Saturday, December 20, 2026
Class times: 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM
Register and Enroll Students Now!

Overview

This trimester invites students to fully immerse themselves in the language, techniques, and spirit of jazz improvisation. Through focused instruction, ensemble work, and guided mentorship, participants will discover how to express themselves with authenticity, creativity, and confidence in the moment.

Students will study master improvisers, learn the building blocks of jazz vocabulary, and explore how to apply their skills across swing, bebop, modal, and contemporary jazz styles. The trimester culminates in a “Live Improvisation Showcase” where students perform alongside faculty and guest artists in spontaneous collaborations.

Core Learning Areas

The Language of Jazz
Melodic development

Call-and-response phrasing

Jazz articulation and nuance

Rhythmic Freedom
Syncopation and swing feel

Odd meters and polyrhythms

Using silence and space

Harmonic Exploration
Chord-scale relationships

Modal improvisation

Playing “inside” vs. “outside”

Listening & Interaction
Active listening in ensemble settings

Responding and supporting other soloists

Developing your own improvisational voice

Guest Artist Spotlight

Each trimester week will include insights and demonstrations from a featured jazz improviser, showing their personal approach and engaging students in Q&A sessions.

Educational Programs

Questions on the best class for you? Contact our team! 

LAS VEGAS YOUTH JAZZ ORCHESTRA

Includes: All music, instruction, professional mentors, JOI Jazz Language classes, comps to JOI events and concerts, and Masterclasses from world-renowned jazz luminaries!

​

Tuition is only $175 per semester!

​

Why join the Las Vegas Youth Jazz Orchestra?
Register

Jammin' with JOI provides students with fun, relaxed, and supportive free summer program. Students from middle through high school join seasoned professional mentors to study and explore jazz language and play with them and other students from across Southern Nevada in a fun, relaxed, and supportive atmosphere. Students do not have to register, can come any time, and are welcome to bring friends. They do not have to be members of Jazz Outreach Initiative's other programs, and all abilities are welcome. HERITAGE SCHOOL OF MUSIC

THE DON “MOOSE” JAMISON HERITAGE SCHOOL OF MUSIC IS THE NEW ORLEANS JAZZ & HERITAGE FOUNDATION’S SIGNATURE EDUCATION PROGRAM.

Since 1990, the Don “Moose” Jamison Heritage School of Music, a free afterschool program, which serves nearly 300 students a week, from beginners aged 8 years old to advanced students aged 18 with in-depth music training, ensemble playing and music theory throughout the school year and summer school taught by some of the best musicians in New Orleans . 

Over the years, the program has experienced significant growth, particularly with the 2014 opening of the George and Joyce Wein Jazz & Heritage Center in New Orleans’ historic Tremé neighborhood, marking the school’s first-ever permanent home. This fully renovated facility boasts seven state-of-the-art classrooms equipped for music instruction, a 200-seat auditorium, and a recording studio, fostering an environment conducive to expanding the program and accommodating more students.

Today, the program also offers classes in audio and studio recording and vocal classes.  Students are accepted into the program at the beginning of school semesters.  The school’s commitment to nurturing young talent and promoting a deep appreciation for music underscores its valuable contribution to the community.

BECOME PART OF THE HERITAGE SCHOOL OF MUSIC FAMILY!

Our programs are free and open to students ages 8 to 18. No prior musical experience is required.

For more information about the Heritage School, feel free to email Andrea Garcés, HSM Administrator, at HSM@jazzandheritage.org.

School Programs & Partnerships
SCHOOL PROGRAMS & PARTNERSHIPS

SFJAZZ brings world-class jazz artists out of the concert hall and into the community, connecting youth and adults, students and professionals, musicians and non-musicians with a diverse array of interactive programs and events. From field trips to our unique SFJAZZ Center Auditorium, to hands on learning in their very own classrooms with jazz professionals, our School Programs give students access to jazz’s rich and critical history.

Our programs support the San Francisco Unified School District’s Arts Education Master Plan to make music education accessible to all.

VIEW BROCHURE

OUR SCHOOL PROGRAMS:

Serve all San Francisco and Oakland public and charter middle schools
Provide over 25,000 hours of instruction each year
Donate over 3,000 SFJAZZ Center concert tickets to public schools and community groups each year
Provide students and educators special access to select interactive soundchecks, rehearsals, concerts and professional development workshops

MAKE A DONATION

SFJAZZ EDUCATION ONLINE

Sign up here to access curriculum materials, exclusive concerts, masterclasses, lesson plans, lectures, and more designed for current and future musicians and audiences. All resources come from the Education team at SFJAZZ, who serve thousands of adults and youth across the Bay Area. Sign up and learn how jazz is alive and thriving!

*All information is confidential. SFJAZZ Education will never share your information with others. For questions, email education@sfjazz.org.

Already signed up? Click below to access exclusive curricular materials.

EDUCATOR PORTAL

JAZZ IN THE MIDDLE

Jazz in the Middle sends jazz musicians and poets into middle school humanities classrooms to unlock the history of jazz from a social, historical, and creative perspective.

MORE

SCHOOL DAY CONCERTS

These free performances are tailored to students in grades K-12 with leading jazz artists and educators at the SFJAZZ Center's beautiful Miner Auditorium, as well as direct to middle schools across San Francisco and Oakland. Students experience jazz in all its forms, participate in a highly interactive environment, and learn how jazz is alive, relevant and continuing to grow today.

Volunteer

Thank you for your interest in volunteering for Kuumbwa Jazz! All volunteer positions are currently filled, but please feel free to complete the application below and be added to the wait-list.

Please click here to apply!

Volunteer-powered since 1975.

A dedicated group of volunteers has powered Kuumbwa’s success for nearly five decades. We are fortunate to be part of a community with such talented and dedicated individuals who are ready, willing, and able to help set the stage for artists from around the world.

Volunteers work in many areas of Kuumbwa Jazz: taking tickets at the door, helping in the café, bar, and gift shop during concerts, assisting the small staff with day-to-day operations throughout the week, and pitching in with special events throughout the year. Thank you for your interest in volunteering!

What is the time commitment for volunteering?

Prospective volunteers are asked to make a one-year commitment. The amount of time volunteered each week depends on the type of task you are interested in. All volunteers are expected to arrive on time ready to work and stay until their shift is completed – our concert schedule depends on it!

What can I do as a volunteer?

You can help with food prep, bar and café service, gift shop sales, dishwashing, venue cleanup, office assistance, special event assistance, and as part of the door crew. 

How do I get started?

Please fill out the volunteer application. We will keep your application on file and contact you when a position opens up.

Jazz Aspen Snowmass Local Education Initiatives

JAS LEI (Local Education Initiatives) develops programming that complements existing public school music programs and replaces programs where schools suffer losses due to budget cuts. These programs are invaluable to students and teachers in the Roaring Fork Valley and 1-70 corridor. Learn more about JAS education programming and history here.

With the opening of the new Paul JAS Center in Dec. 2025, JAS will be expanding current programming into exciting new opportunities, including classes and workshops for preschoolers, additional summer camps and after-school programming, music recording classes and more.

Since 1996 JAS has donated over $11 million to these and other education initiatives! Visit us here for news & updates on JAS LEI Programming, including info on the 2026 Street Horns Auditions and JAS Summer Camps!

JAS Street Horns

Sponsored by Jazz Aspen Snowmass, the JAS Street Horns program is for advanced Middle and High School musicians interested in a high-level band experience with their peers from across the Western Slope.

Led by Basalt Band Director Chance Davis, alongside JAS In-Schools Director Chris Bank, additional JAS In-Schools Faculty, and visiting professional jazz musicians, the Street Horns is comprised of students across the Western Slope of Colorado.

The Programs of The Carr Center

The Carr Center is a multi-disciplinary arts organization that leverages the essence of the African American cultural experience to inspire, entertain, challenge and educate.

Currently, our three core  programs include :

The Carr Center Artist Hub:  Home to local and regional artists as well as special guest artist residencies.  The Carr Center hub provides support and space for resident artists, community-based artists and arts organizations to do and/or create their work 
The Carr Center Presents: Hosts national, regional and local performing and visual arts to metro-Detroit.  These series of LIVE performance, film and visual arts events are also available to the public via Livestream.
The Carr Center Arts Academy: Our educational umbrella which offers multi-disciplinary arts education and training through in-school classes, summer intensives and early career professional development programs. 

Programs include a Saturday Arts Academy for students grades 6 – 8, our competitive Summer Dance Intensive, offered  through a partnership with the Debbie Allen Dance Academy and  professional development programs for early-career artists, includingThe Gathering Orchestra, and the Independent Scholars Program for visual artists.

And Something’s Coming… 

Even before the current health crisis, The Carr Center had been exploring the need for an intimate performance studio, providing broadcast-quality infrastructure and post-production. Then came the pandemic and suddenly staying connected to our audience, in the absence of normal activity, became our number one priority.

We diligently began to create a new business model. One that reflects the new realities around LIVE audience engagement. Our new performance studio is at the very core of that model. Once the studio opens, later this year, all of our performances and educational programs will include digital content as fundamental elements. Using the performance studio we will engage our audience in three ways.

Volunteer

At the Carr Center, volunteers will be a key part of our success…

Whether welcoming patrons before a performance, providing the public with information about the Carr, ushering patrons to their seats, or performing many other vital tasks, our volunteers give the Carr its community identity. As our most visible hosts and hostesses, their primary goal is to make every experience enjoyable and memorable for our guests.

Volunteers are involved in events, participate in activities, receive meaningful assignments, and get recognition for work well done.

We know that, without our dedicated volunteers, the vibrant, warm atmosphere that makes Carr Center events so special would not be possible.

General Requirements

The essential requirements to become a volunteer are an interest and enthusiasm for the performing arts, a willingness to serve all patrons of the Carr Center with care and respect, a high level of congeniality in serving our guests, a professional demeanor, and punctuality in all assignments. Volunteers must be 16 years of age or older. Volunteers are needed to serve as performance ushers, education program ushers, and exhibition monitors.

It is the individual’s willingness to serve that makes the volunteer program successful. Your acceptance of volunteering indicates an agreement to fulfill the responsibility for active participation and affirms your support of the principles and ideals of the Carr Center and all its activities.

Become a Volunteer

We would like to hear from any and all in our community who have a strong interest and some time to serve on a volunteer staff for the Carr Center. Those with previous volunteer experience in this field are especially welcome to apply. We will respond to all who inquire.

If you are interested in volunteering please contact us via email sarah@thecarrcenter.org  or you can call us directly at 313 634 4852 and leave a message.

content.text:
### Overview of Open Evidence Tabs

The following 12 tabs have been left open in the browser for your direct review, representing a balanced mix of program descriptions, social impact initiatives, youth education, and volunteer/support portals:

1. **Tab ID 2017691952** — *What We Do - Jazz Foundation of America*  
   URL: `https://jazzfoundation.org/what-we-do/` (Focus: Emergency housing, pro-bono medical care, elder outreach, school gigs)
2. **Tab ID 2017691953** — *Education and Community Engagement — Preservation Hall Foundation*  
   URL: `https://www.preshallfoundation.org/education` (Focus: K–12 New Orleans brass band curricula, school field trips, free community concerts)
3. **Tab ID 2017691954** — *About Us — Seattle JazzED*  
   URL: `https://www.seattlejazzed.org/aboutus` (Focus: Pay-what-you-can sliding-scale music access, youth development, gender equity in jazz)
4. **Tab ID 2017691955** — *Jazzmobile, Inc.*  
   URL: `https://jazzmobile.org/` (Focus: Free neighborhood mobile stage concerts, Title I school lecture-demonstrations, Saturday Jazz Workshop)
5. **Tab ID 2017691956** — *Education – The Philadelphia Clef Club of Jazz & Performing Arts*  
   URL: `https://clefclubofjazz.org/education` (Focus: Youth prep academy, intergenerational jazz master mentorship, performance scholarships)
6. **Tab ID 2017691957** — *Volunteer | Jazz Outreach Initiative*  
   URL: `https://www.jazzoutreachinitiative.org/jja` (Focus: Hands-on volunteer wing "JOI Jazz Alliance", youth orchestra, Title 1 school clinics)
7. **Tab ID 2017691958** — *Volunteer Opportunities - The New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival and Foundation, Inc.*  
   URL: `https://www.jazzandheritage.org/volunteer-opportunities/` (Focus: Year-round civic volunteering, free music academy, community grants)
8. **Tab ID 2017691959** — *SFJAZZ.org | School Programs & Partnerships*  
   URL: `https://www.sfjazz.org/education/school-programs-partnerships/` (Focus: Free public school day concerts, "Jazz in the Middle" humanities integration)
9. **Tab ID 2017691960** — *Volunteer - Kuumbwa Jazz*  
   URL: `https://www.kuumbwajazz.org/volunteer/` (Focus: Dedicated grassroots volunteer staffing, honor band, student masterclasses)
10. **Tab ID 2017691961** — *Labor Day Experience: Vendor & Volunteer Opportunities | Jazz Aspen Snowmass*  
    URL: `https://jazzaspensnowmass.org/labor-day-experience/volunteer-and-vending/` (Focus: Community volunteer program, public school music replacement, free community nights)
11. **Tab ID 2017691962** — *Volunteer - the Carr Center*  
    URL: `https://www.thecarrcenter.org/support/volunteer/` (Focus: Community arts ushering/hospitality volunteering, Gathering Orchestra fellowship, youth arts academy)
12. **Tab ID 2017691963** — *Our Jazz Education Programs - Hancock Institute of Jazz*  
    URL: `https://hancockinstitute.org/education/` (Focus: Free nationwide public school jazz curriculum, Peer-to-Peer public high school tours)

*(Note: Tab ID 2017691829 remains the initial Google search anchor tab).*

---

### Profile of 12 Jazz Nonprofits & Community Programs

#### 1. Jazz Foundation of America (JFA)
- **Location:** New York, NY (Operates nationally across the U.S.)
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Housing & Emergency Assistance:* Prevents homelessness and evictions for elder, ill, and struggling jazz and blues musicians by paying back rents, mortgages, utility bills, and emergency living expenses.
  2. *Pro Bono Medical Care & Disaster Relief:* Partners with Englewood Hospital and a national network of medical specialists to provide free consultations, treatments, and surgical care for uninsured musicians; provides emergency rebuilding grants and instrument replacement after natural catastrophes (e.g., Gulf Coast hurricanes).
  3. *Jazz & Blues in the Schools / Nursing Homes / The Gig Fund:* Hires out-of-work and elder musicians to perform interactive educational concerts in inner-city public schools and therapeutic jazz performances in nursing homes/assisted-living facilities (including memory care and Alzheimer’s wards), alongside free pop-up neighborhood concerts.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown as a general public volunteer sign-up program on their site (medical professionals volunteer via hospital partnerships, but general community volunteer shifts are not listed).
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation system (one-time, monthly, legacy gifts).
  - *Attending:* Visible public events (annual Great Night in Harlem gala, Loft Party, Monday Night Jam).
  - *Partnering:* Visible institutional partnerships with hospitals, corporate donors, and community centers.

#### 2. Preservation Hall Foundation
- **Location:** New Orleans, LA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Free Digital Curricula & Sheet Music ("Preservation Hall Lessons" & "Brass Bandbook"):* Provides K–12 educators nationwide with free classroom lesson plans and 12-part traditional brass band arrangements with historical context to preserve Black American musical traditions.
  2. *"Kids in the Hall" Field Trips & Open Soundchecks:* Brings local students on free, interactive field trips to Preservation Hall for live performance and musician Q&A; offers free open soundchecks and clinics in 100% of cities visited by the touring band.
  3. *Free Community Concerts & The Sousafund:* Presents free outdoor family concerts in New Orleans neighborhoods with limited economic access to live cultural institutions, and provides brass/sousaphone instruments and mentorship to Orleans and Jefferson Parish students in need.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown (no volunteer sign-up portal on their site).
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation platform (one-time, recurring, and "Pass It On" capital campaign).
  - *Attending:* Visible concert calendar for historic Preservation Hall and free community outreach events.
  - *Partnering:* Visible collaboration channels for visiting educators, schools, and cultural institutions.

#### 3. Seattle JazzED
- **Location:** Seattle, WA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Sliding-Scale Tuition & Free Instrument Loans:* Operates on a "choose-your-tuition-level" model with no-questions-asked 100% tuition waivers and free instrument loans, ensuring family income is never a barrier to musical training.
  2. *Equity-Centered Youth Ensembles:* Delivers structured instrumental training from ages 8 months through 12th grade (JazzSprouts, Foundations, Connections, Explorations, Summer Jazz Ambassadors) pairing musicianship with life mentorship.
  3. *Femme Ellington Project & Gender-Expansive Initiatives:* Programs explicitly created to address historical gender disparities in jazz, offering all-city girls/non-binary ensembles, masterclasses, and an annual "Femme: Women & Gender-Expansive Jazz Day."
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown as an ongoing drop-in volunteer role (they have a visible "Join the Board" application, but general volunteer sign-up is not shown).
  - *Donating:* Visible donation portal (one-time, monthly, Jazz Futures Fund, workplace matching).
  - *Attending:* Visible calendar of student concerts, open rehearsals, masterclasses, and guest clinician workshops.
  - *Partnering:* Visible school district partnership offerings (Black History Month assemblies, school clinics, teacher toolkits).

#### 4. Jazzmobile
- **Location:** New York, NY (Harlem / All 5 Boroughs)
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Free Mobile Summerfest Concerts:* Founded in 1964 by Dr. Billy Taylor, Jazzmobile brings custom-built mobile stage concerts directly to streets, parks, public housing complexes, and senior centers in historically underserved neighborhoods across all five NYC boroughs.
  2. *In-School Lecture Demonstrations ("Jazz in the First Person"):* Dispatches professional jazz artists to New York City public elementary, middle, and high schools for free 45-to-60-minute interactive music history presentations.
  3. *Saturday Jazz Workshop (SJW):* Operates long-running, accessible weekend music training (hosted at Wadleigh Secondary School in Central Harlem), teaching jazz harmony, improvisation, ensemble technique, and theory to youth and emerging artists.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown (no volunteer application or portal visible; only direct office contact info).
  - *Donating:* Visible PayPal donation link on their site.
  - *Attending:* Visible public Summerfest schedule (all outdoor concerts are free to the public).
  - *Partnering:* Visible co-presentations with NYC Parks, Central Park Conservancy, Harlem Stage, and the Apollo Theater.

#### 5. Philadelphia Clef Club of Jazz & Performing Arts
- **Location:** Philadelphia, PA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Clef Preparatory Jazz Music Academy (CPJMA):* Delivers intensive Saturday music instruction (9:00 AM – 3:00 PM) for youth covering ear training, polyrhythms, jazz theory, and spontaneous improvisation.
  2. *Auditioned Youth Music Scholarships:* Awards need- and merit-based financial aid in voice, piano, and instrumental studies to ensure students ages 13–18 can access private lessons and ensemble coaching.
  3. *Community Masterclasses & Civic Band Bookings:* Preserves Philadelphia’s Black jazz legacy (descending from the historic Black musicians' union Local 274) through public masterclasses, cultural symposiums, and a "Request a Band" program that connects youth ensembles with civic events.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown (no volunteer portal; inquiries directed through administrative phone/email).
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation system (Zeffy platform and Capital Improvement Campaign).
  - *Attending:* Visible concert series, Diamond Year celebrations, student showcases, and live-streams.
  - *Partnering:* Visible "Cultural Collaborations at the Clef" framework for arts organizations, schools, and venue rentals.

#### 6. Jazz Outreach Initiative (JOI)
- **Location:** Las Vegas, NV
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Title 1 School Outreach & "Jazz Routes":* Delivers in-school clinics, workshops, and instrument loans specifically targeting economically disadvantaged and at-risk youth in Clark County Title 1 schools.
  2. *Las Vegas Youth Jazz Orchestra (LVYJO) & "Jammin' with JOI":* Provides low-cost semester-based ensemble training ($175/semester with professional mentors) alongside a 100% free summer drop-in program where students of any skill level can learn jazz language without advance registration.
  3. *Band Director Academy & Regional Festival:* Organizes regional educational festivals (including regional Essentially Ellington festivals) and teacher-training academies to give local public school band directors practical jazz pedagogy tools.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* **Visible and active.** JOI maintains a dedicated volunteer wing called the **"JOI Jazz Alliance"** with an open online sign-up form for community members to help with concerts, youth orchestra support, and outreach programs.
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation processing and corporate sponsorship tiers.
  - *Attending:* Visible calendar featuring youth orchestra concerts and professional Jazz Vegas Orchestra performances.
  - *Partnering:* Visible school district, corporate, and community church venue partnerships.

#### 7. New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation
- **Location:** New Orleans, LA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Don "Moose" Jamison Heritage School of Music:* Provides completely tuition-free afterschool and weekend music education for ~300 youth weekly (ages 8–18) at the George & Joyce Wein Jazz & Heritage Center in Tremé, including instrument classes, vocal workshops, and audio production.
  2. *Community Partnership Grants & Catapult Fund:* Reinvests proceeds from the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival directly into Louisiana communities, distributing millions in grants to schools, independent musicians, and cultural non-profits, plus business accelerator grants for creative entrepreneurs.
  3. *Free Community Cultural Festivals & Outreach Tickets:* Organizes admission-free community festivals (Congo Square Rhythms, Crescent City Blues & BBQ, Class Got Brass competition) and distributes thousands of free Jazz Fest tickets to low-income families and neighborhood groups.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* **Visible and active.** Features a dedicated "Volunteer Opportunities" portal with an online profile application for individuals 18+ to work on community outreach, educational programs, and festival operations year-round.
  - *Donating:* Visible donation portal (Jazz & Heritage Circle, general foundation gifts).
  - *Attending:* Visible calendar of free community festivals, Heritage School concerts, and Wein Center performances.
  - *Partnering:* Visible formal grant application portal (Community Partnership Grants) and corporate sponsorship opportunities.

#### 8. SFJAZZ (Education & Community Programs)
- **Location:** San Francisco, CA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Public School Day Concerts & Middle School Outreach:* Delivers interactive jazz concerts free of charge to K–12 students at Miner Auditorium and directly inside public/charter middle schools across San Francisco and Oakland.
  2. *"Jazz in the Middle" Humanities Integration:* Sends professional jazz musicians and poets directly into middle school humanities classrooms to teach jazz history, civil rights connections, and creative writing, contributing to SFUSD’s Arts Education Master Plan.
  3. *Ticket Donation Program & Pre-Professional Ensembles:* Donates more than 3,000 concert tickets annually to public schools and community organizations, and runs the auditioned SFJAZZ High School All-Stars alongside free Community Jam Sessions.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown on the live site (volunteer page returns a 404 error; no open public volunteer portal).
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation platform supporting the Education and Artist Funds.
  - *Attending:* Visible public performance calendar, Family Matinees, and free Community Jams.
  - *Partnering:* Visible Educator Portal and institutional partnerships with Bay Area public school districts.

#### 9. Kuumbwa Jazz
- **Location:** Santa Cruz, CA
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Volunteer-Operated Community Performance Center:* Operates a dedicated nonprofit cultural hub where community members assist with venue operations, artist hospitality, and box office, keeping world-class jazz accessible in Santa Cruz.
  2. *Kuumbwa Jazz Honor Band:* Provides a free, audition-based honor ensemble for high school musicians across Santa Cruz and Monterey counties, offering professional coaching and public concert exposure.
  3. *Free Masterclasses, Camp Scholarships & "Discover Jazz":* Hosts free artist masterclasses for students prior to evening concerts, provides financial need scholarships for its annual Summer Jazz Camp, and conducts "Discover Jazz" public lecture series.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* **Visible and active.** Explicit "Volunteer" page explaining their 50-year volunteer-powered model (ushers, box office, café, special events) with an online application form and waitlist.
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation and annual membership options.
  - *Attending:* Visible year-round concert calendar with student discount pricing.
  - *Partnering:* Visible corporate sponsorship and civic venue rental options.

#### 10. Jazz Aspen Snowmass (JAS)
- **Location:** Aspen & Roaring Fork Valley, CO
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *JAS In-Schools & Local Education Initiatives (LEI):* Directly replaces and supplements public school music programs cut by school district budget shortfalls across the Roaring Fork Valley and I-70 corridor (having invested over $11 million in local education since 1996).
  2. *JAS Street Horns & Summer Music Camps:* Sponsors a high-level ensemble for middle and high school brass/woodwind students from Colorado's Western Slope, paired with summer camps in brass playing and beatmaking/recording at the Paul JAS Center.
  3. *Free Community Nights & JAS Academy:* Hosts weekly free Tuesday Community Nights (local showcases, open mic nights, educational gatherings) at the Paul JAS Center, and provides full-scholarship pre-professional training for emerging jazz artists via the JAS Academy.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* **Visible and active.** Dedicated "Volunteer Opportunities" application (volunteers age 16+ commit to festival/event shifts in exchange for event admission and apparel; coordinated via `volunteer@jazzaspensnowmass.org`).
  - *Donating:* Visible "Keep the Music Playing" capital campaign and annual giving forms.
  - *Attending:* Visible tickets for mainstage festivals, JAS Café, and free Tuesday Community Nights.
  - *Partnering:* Visible school district collaborations, local food/craft vendor applications, and corporate sponsorships.

#### 11. The Carr Center
- **Location:** Detroit, MI
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *The Carr Center Arts Academy & Saturday Programs:* Offers multi-disciplinary African American arts and jazz education for middle school youth (grades 6–8) through in-school programs and weekend academies.
  2. *The Gathering Orchestra Professional Fellowship:* Operates a two-year paid fellowship and professional development residency for early-career jazz artists (ages 18–28) under the direction of bassist Rodney Whitaker.
  3. *Community Hub & Accessible Performances:* Serves Detroit neighborhoods by providing subsidized creative space for resident artists and presenting free/low-cost live and streamed concerts at accessible civic spaces (such as The Shepherd, Belle Isle's Dossin Museum, and local cathedrals).
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* **Visible and active.** Dedicated "Volunteer" page seeking community members (age 16+) to serve as performance ushers, educational program assistants, and gallery docents (contact via email `sarah@thecarrcenter.org` or phone).
  - *Donating:* Visible online donation system ("DONATE NOW" via ppay.co).
  - *Attending:* Visible calendar of gallery exhibits, livestreams, and live concerts across Detroit.
  - *Partnering:* Visible creative partnerships (e.g., Debbie Allen Dance Academy, Detroit School of Arts).

#### 12. Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz
- **Location:** Washington, DC & Los Angeles, CA (Operates nationally and internationally)
- **3+ Concrete Ways It Serves the Community:**
  1. *Jazz in America (National Public School Curriculum):* Operates `jazzinamerica.org`, providing a free, comprehensive jazz and civil rights curriculum for 5th, 8th, and 11th grade public school social studies and music teachers nationwide.
  2. *Peer-to-Peer Public School Tours:* Selects student jazz sextets from specialized public performing arts high schools to tour regular public schools across other states, delivering student-led interactive assemblies, clinics, and jam sessions that promote creative discipline and non-violence.
  3. *"BeBop to Hip-Hop" & International Jazz Day Outreach:* Engages urban youth by linking classic jazz improvisation to hip-hop beatmaking and spoken word, and partners with UNESCO to lead International Jazz Day educational programming reaching thousands of communities worldwide.
- **Involvement Options:**
  - *Volunteering:* Not shown on their public website (program delivery relies on staff, teaching artists, and student fellows).
  - *Donating:* Visible online contribution portal (`hancockinstitute.org/contribute/`).
  - *Attending:* Visible public event notices, competition galas, and global livestreams.
  - *Partnering:* Visible corporate sponsor programs and institutional partnerships with school districts, UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music, and UNESCO.

---

### Synthesis and Model Comparison

#### Grouping by Community Service Model

1. **Direct Social Safety Net & Musician Welfare:**
   - *Organizations:* **Jazz Foundation of America (JFA)**.
   - *Focus:* Treats jazz artists as vulnerable community cultural elders. Instead of viewing jazz strictly as a performance product, this model provides emergency housing stipends, free hospital surgeries, disaster rebuilding, and pays musicians to bring music to Alzheimer's wards and Title I classrooms.
2. **Tuition-Free & Sliding-Scale Youth Development Centers:**
   - *Organizations:* **Seattle JazzED**, **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation (Heritage School of Music)**, **Philadelphia Clef Club**, **Jazz Outreach Initiative (JOI)**.
   - *Focus:* Removes the financial barrier to learning an instrument. They provide free instrument loan libraries, afterschool/weekend training, and explicit sliding-scale or 100% tuition-free models to ensure low-income and underrepresented youth can access high-level instruction.
3. **Public School System Supplementation & In-Classroom Integration:**
   - *Organizations:* **SFJAZZ**, **Jazz Aspen Snowmass (JAS In-Schools)**, **Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz**.
   - *Focus:* Directly targets budget shortfalls in public education. They either replace eliminated music classes in rural/mountain corridors, integrate jazz into standard middle school history and humanities classes, or supply free nationwide curriculum materials.
4. **Civic Space Activation & Grassroots Cultural Preserves:**
   - *Organizations:* **Jazzmobile**, **Preservation Hall Foundation**, **Kuumbwa Jazz**, **The Carr Center**.
   - *Focus:* Reclaiming public space and cultural history. They bring free mobile concert stages into low-income public parks and housing complexes, preserve historic African American cultural unions and traditional New Orleans brass traditions, and operate community-staffed cultural hubs.

#### Most Common vs. Most Distinctive Approaches

- **Most Common Approaches:**
  - *In-School Masterclasses & Field Trips:* Nearly every organization brings musicians into schools or brings students into concert halls (e.g., SFJAZZ School Day Concerts, Preservation Hall's "Kids in the Hall", Jazzmobile's "Jazz in the First Person").
  - *Auditioned Youth Honors/Ensemble Academies:* Providing pre-professional training for teenagers with financial aid or free tuition (e.g., Clef Prep, LVYJO, Kuumbwa Honor Band, SFJAZZ All-Stars).
- **Most Distinctive Approaches:**
  - *Healthcare & Homelessness Intervention as Arts Preservation (Jazz Foundation of America):* Addressing social determinants of health (pro-bono hospital care, paying back rent) to keep musicians alive and sheltered.
  - *Gender Equity in Jazz Pedagogy (Seattle JazzED):* The "Femme Ellington Project" and gender-expansive jazz camps specifically dismantle the historical male dominance of jazz brass and rhythm sections.
  - *Peer-to-Peer Youth Diplomacy (Herbie Hancock Institute):* Using talented public high schoolers from one region to teach and inspire students in another state, teaching jazz as an exercise in democracy and conflict resolution.
  - *Mobile Stage Neighborhood Deployment (Jazzmobile):* Eliminating transportation and ticketing barriers by physically driving concerts into housing projects, public street corners, and neighborhood parks.
  - *Festival Reinvestment into Micro-Grants (New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation):* Using commercial festival profits to fund micro-grants for local neighborhood artists and cultural small businesses.

---

### Ranked Top 5 Recommendations for Hands-On Community Impact

For an outsider looking to get involved through hands-on volunteering, impactful donations, or community-serving partnerships, these are the 5 strongest organizations:

#### 1. Seattle JazzED (Ranked #1 — Overall Hands-on Youth Impact)
- **Why:** They have created the most intentional, barrier-free community music school model in the country. Their commitment to 100% tuition sliding scales (no proof of income required), free instrument checkouts, and programs targeting historically underrepresented young women and non-binary youth makes every dollar and hour directly transform a young person's daily life.
- **Best For Designation:** **Best for Youth Education Impact**

#### 2. Jazz Outreach Initiative (JOI) (Ranked #2 — Most Accessible Hands-on Volunteer Gateway)
- **Why:** Unlike many established jazz institutions that restrict public participation to passive financial donations, JOI built a structured, welcoming community volunteer wing (**The JOI Jazz Alliance**). A community member can directly apply on their site to support Title 1 school clinics, youth orchestra logistics, and community jams, making it ideal for someone who wants to roll up their sleeves immediately.
- **Best For Designation:** **Best for Volunteering**

#### 3. Jazzmobile (Ranked #3 — Purest Broader Community Outreach)
- **Why:** For 60 years, Jazzmobile has maintained the purest neighborhood-level outreach model in urban America. By mounting concerts on mobile stages in public parks, senior centers, and public housing courtyards where people gather, they eliminate economic, cultural, and geographic gatekeeping, making world-class music a free public utility.
- **Best For Designation:** **Best for Broader Community Outreach**

#### 4. Jazz Foundation of America (JFA) (Ranked #4 — Strongest Social Safety Net & Human Impact)
- **Why:** If you want your philanthropic support to prevent immediate human suffering, JFA is unmatched. They directly resolve evictions, coordinate life-saving pro-bono surgeries, and provide emergency relief checks to aging musicians who created American roots music, while simultaneously employing them to perform in memory-care facilities and underfunded schools.

#### 5. New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation (Ranked #5 — Best Systemic Community Investment Model)
- **Why:** They combine free, high-caliber year-round youth education (Heritage School of Music) with systemic community wealth-building. Because they operate active year-round volunteer programs and distribute direct grants to local artists and schools, they represent the gold standard for how cultural assets can be reinvested into a city's social fabric.

Education and Community Engagement

Music education is at the core of our mission to protect, preserve and perpetuate New Orleans musical traditions. Passing on the knowledge of this music to the next generation of New Orleans musicians is a primary focus of the Preservation Hall Foundation, as well as a personal focus and passion of many of the beloved musicians of Preservation Hall. 

Over the COVID-19 pandemic, we launched Preservation Hall Lessons, offering students and educators free digital learning materials and classroom-ready lesson plans on New Orleans music and culture. Today, we are thrilled to resume in-person education programming like Kids in the Hall at Preservation Hall, and in partnership with music organizations around the country – providing unforgettable, experiential settings for students, learning by playing, and experiencing lasting mentorship with musicians, tradition bearers, and teaching artists from the Preservation Hall collective of musicians.

DONATE THROUGH GIVENOLA DAY!
SUPPORT NEW ORLEANS MUSIC EDUCATION→
Programs
Learning the New Orleans Way: 
Preservation Hall Lessons

The Preservation Hall Foundation has developed Preservation Hall Lessons: a free, online resource bank for teachers and music educators. The Lessons website includes a range of complete lesson plans for grades K-12, focusing on New Orleans style music, particularly traditional New Orleans Jazz and brass band music. The Lessons website is not just for regional use – it is now available for educators across the nation to help articulate the living art forms that exist in New Orleans on a national level, and ensure its inclusion in music education.

EXPLORE PRESERVATION HALL LESSONS
SUBSCRIBE FOR EMAIL UPDATES ON PHLESSONS
Brass Bandbook

The Preservation Hall Foundation Brass Bandbook is a free online resource for musicians and educators – complete with sheet music of 12 classic New Orleans tunes, like “Bourbon Street Parade and “Lil’ Liza Jane.” Complete with lyrics and historical context of the songs, this free sheet music is available for clarinet, trumpet, trombone, tuba, tenor sax, snare drum and bass drum at preshallfoundation.org/brassbandbook. 

ACCESS THE BRASS BANDBOOK→
Kids in the Hall

Classroom lessons come to life with the Preservation Hall Foundation's Kids in the Hall Field Trip program. In this one-hour field trip, students engage and listen to a Preservation Hall Band, as well as have an opportunity for a Q&A session with members of the Preservation Hall Collective. 

SIGN UP FOR A KIDS IN THE HALL FIELD TRIP →
Workshops, Masterclasses, and Open Soundchecks 

The Preservation Hall Foundation provides workshops, masterclasses, and open soundchecks to schools in the Greater New Orleans area and around the U.S., focusing on Brass Band and Traditional New Orleans Jazz. Open soundchecks are offered on 100% of the Preservation Hall Jazz Band's touring dates.  

To schedule a workshop or masterclass or to join us at an open soundcheck on any of Preservation Hall Jazz Band’s tour dates, email info@preshallfoundation.org.

Community Concerts

Community Concerts provides a range of free concerts in the Greater New Orleans area for communities limited in access to Preservation Hall by distance, economics, or other circumstances. These free concerts are performed by members of the Preservation Hall Collective and are designed for the whole family to attend. 

Stay tuned to our Facebook page for more details about upcoming concert performances. 

FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK →
FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM →
Sousafund

In the wake of Ben Jaffe's Sousaphone being stolen, the Sousafund was established in 2018 to provide young bass and sousaphone students with high quality instruments. Students in Orleans and Jefferson Parish have received instruments and mentorship on upright bass or sousaphone.

Seattle JazzED Programs Overview:
 REGISTER FOR FALL PROGRAMS TODAY!

 
About/ Academic Year Programs/ Events/ Learning Resources/ JazzED + Schools/ Support/ Contact
Programs Overview
Programs
JazzSprouts

JazzSprouts is a jazz education program designed for children 8 months to five years old. Our 45-minute classes engage both the child and caregiver, through live music, dancing, story time and a racially-diverse curriculum. Families learn about core musical concepts, instruments, and great performers of Jazz, a vital Black American art form.

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Jazz Jumpers

Students K-3 will explore the core elements of music through the lens of jazz. Through singing, movement, and hands-on instrument discovery, young musicians will learn about the rich history of artists, their iconic styles, and the cultural roots that shaped this uniquely American art form.

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Foundations

Our Foundations class is for beginners in grades 4-8 with no previous music experience! Your budding musician will learn in with others in instrument groups built for individual learning and relationship building. We’ll teach you what you need to know about your instrument of choice in this class designed to support your musician for as many quarters as they need to feel confident on their instrument!

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Connections

Connections is for intermediate students in grades 5-8 who are proficient on their instrument and ready to grow as a jazz musician. Students will get lots of time to play their instrument. Classes focus on learning easy jazz tunes by ear, focused listening, ear-training, exploring rhythmic and creative concepts, and more!

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER
Explorations

Explorations is designed for musicians in grades 9 and above and is all about, well, exploring! Now that you are comfortable making music with your instrument, is there a particular topic that seems interesting? Maybe you want to play gigs but don’t know how to start, or maybe you want to dig in to modern jazz, or Latin music! Explorations includes a variety of classes of varying skill levels, so there’s something for everyone. 

LEARN MORE AND REGISTER

We are dedicated to creating a safe environment for our students, families, educators, and administrative staff as we welcome you to our programs. For our latest health and safety protocols, click here.

Seattle JazzED About Us text:
 REGISTER FOR FALL PROGRAMS TODAY!

 
About/ Academic Year Programs/ Events/ Learning Resources/ JazzED + Schools/ Support/ Contact
About Us
Seattle JazzED is YOUR home for excellent music education. 
We believe any student who wants to play should get to play. Maybe that’s you?

A bit about us. At Seattle JazzED we welcome students in grades K-12 at all levels. You can play or sing in an ensemble, take a one-day workshop, spend a week in the summer honing skills…or all three!

You may already know Seattle JazzED from some of our one-of-a-kind programs: The New Works Ensemble directed by composer Wayne Horvitz; or the Femme Ellington Project, Seattle's premier all-city girls' jazz band; or maybe Summer Jazz Ambassadors, a tour-de-force ensemble with training in performance skills and mentoring. 

Or maybe you’ve never heard of us until now. That’s cool too!

Here’s what you need to know: Any student can start their instrumental or vocal music education at Seattle JazzED and continue through high school graduation. We’ll take you the whole way. 

Do you already play music, or sing, and have for years? We’ve got plenty of opportunities for you too. 

If you need help figuring out where you fit in, contact us. We’d love to help you. 

P.S. Don’t let cost keep you from participating. At Seattle JazzED you always choose your tuition level. Flexible payment plans and full tuition waivers are also available, no questions asked. We’re able to offer sliding scale prices because our community of families pay what they can and our community of donors give what they can.  

You might be wondering: Why should I play jazz?

Good question! So glad you asked. We love jazz*  because it’s a quintessential Black American art form shared across America and the world. 

What’s more, in jazz you get to improvise and interpret music. It’s a powerful way to express yourself! With jazz you collaborate with your bandmates—you are responsible to each other and the performance you’re working toward. Because jazz is an improvisational music, you get comfortable with taking some creative risks and trying out new ideas. Jazz requires you to get curious, focus in and listen closely to your peers (and they’ll do the same for you.)

[For more on ‘Why Jazz’, watch the video with Wynton Marsalis above. IT’S GOOD.] 

Plus we have a lot of jazz history here! As a JazzED student you’re in league with Seattle’s rich jazz tradition, which stretches from Seattle’s early Jackson Street jazz scene with Ray Charles, Quincy Jones, and Ernestine Anderson, to the smooth jazz of Kenny G, through to the improvisational jazz of Wayne Horvitz, Bill Frisell, and Industrial Revelation. You can be part of this legacy. We’d love to have you.

</untrusted_web_content>

                                Jazzmobile's mission is to present, preserve, promote and propagate America's classical music, Jazz. Founded in 1964 by National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Master, pianist, Dr. Billy Taylor and philanthropist and arts administrator, Ms. Daphne Anstein, Jazzmobile is the first U.S. not-for-profit arts and cultural organization created just for Jazz.  Since the beginning, we have been bringing high quality Jazz performances and education programs to area residents, tourists and other visitors, reaching over 4,000,000 people living or visiting New York City. Our national programs brought us to other cities in the US; and the 'Super Jazz Band' had us touring cities in Europe and Japan.
                                Whether on the street, in a park or at a major concert hall here or abroad, Jazzmobile works in partnership with like-minded organizations to present high quality Jazz performances that enrich the culture and imbue new life into the surrounding area. 
                                Our workshops, master classes, lecture demonstrations, and arts enrichment programs train the next generation of Jazz vocalists and musicians; while also exposing youth to this vibrant art form. For jazz aficionados and other enthusiasts, our panel discussions increase the knowledge of our many adult followers. Our primary aim is to reach out to communities where Jazz was nurtured and new forms born.
                                We are very proud of being an inspiration to other organizations such as The Manchester Craftsman's Guild and Jazz at Lincoln Center.

                                Among Jazzmobile's numerous awards and special citations are:

                                    National Jazz Museum in Harlem & Great Harlem Chamber of Commerce 'Award for Excellence'

                                     'Jazzmobile Salutes Richard Rogers Day' (Mayor Bloomberg)
                                
                            

                            
                                Jazzmobile has reached national and international audiences, touring locally, regionally, across the United States, Europe, Asia and Canada, and performing at such events as:
                                
                                    Created Jazzmobile's and Central Park Conservancy's Annual 'Great Jazz on the Great Hill'
                                    New York City's longest continuous Jazz Festival : SUMMERFEST | Over 50 Years--We commissioned Wycliffe Gordon to create new music to the silent film 'Within Our Gates' by African-American filmmaker Oscar Micheaux. It was premiered with a live orchestra in August 2011 at Columbia University's Miller Theatre and we presented it again in 2013 at Symphony Space where it was recorded.  On April 1, 2016 - Gordon released his long awaited soundtrack Within These Gates of Mine.
                                    The first JAZZ performance at Lincoln Center Out-of-Doors--Under the direction of Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts Leonard de Paur, the creator of Lincoln Center Out of Doors, we presented its 1st Jazz program in 1964. 
                                    The Winnipeg Art Gallery Program
                                    1980 Winter Olympic Games, Lake Placid--NEA Jazz master (saxophone) Frank Foster (1928-2011) was commissioned to compose 'Lake Placid Suite' which was premiered during the Olympic games.  It was later broadcasted via live satellite on Billy Taylor's  NPR 'Jazz Alive,' with a performance by the 23 piece Jazzmobile All-Star Orchestra.
                                    Silver Bridge Concert celebrating Sister Cities New York and Tokyo--A once in a lifetime celebration performance at Lincoln Center's Alice Tully Hall.
                                    'Super Jazz Band' International and National Tour produced by Jazzmobile
                                
                            
                            Our concerts featuring acclaimed performers make musical magic, bringing Jazz to the streets and schools, parks and performance halls. Duke Ellington, Count Basie and Sarah Vaughan are some of the legends who have performed with Jazzmobile, as have:
